verses.1: When I heal Israel, the guilt of Ephraim will be revealed, and the wickedness of Samaria will be exposed, for they practiced deception; a thief will come in, and a band of robbers will strike along the road.
verses.2: Yet they will not say in their hearts: “All our evil has been remembered now.” Now they are surrounded by their own schemes, which have appeared before me.
verses.3: In their wickedness they will rejoice the king, and in their lies they will exalt the rulers.
verses.4: All of them are adulterers, like a furnace heated by the baker, burning from the flame, feeding on fat until it is leavened.
verses.5: On the day of our kings the rulers became drunk; anger from wine led their hand to violence.
verses.6: For their hearts have burned like a furnace; all night they rage, the one who bakes them sleeps briefly by morning, and he ignites like a flaming fire.
verses.7: All of them have burned like a furnace, and they have devoured their judges. All their kings have fallen; none among them calls to me.
verses.8: Ephraim has been confused among the nations; Ephraim has become a vessel without turning.
verses.9: Strangers devoured his strength, and he did not know it; old age came upon him, and he did not know it.
verses.10: And the glory of Israel will be humiliated in his face, yet they will not return to the LORD their God, nor will they seek him in all this.
verses.11: And Ephraim has become like a senseless dove, with no heart; Egypt they called, and to Assyria they went.
verses.12: As they go, I will spread a net over them, like a bird of the heavens, and I will bring them down. I will punish them when they hear the distress of the assembly.
verses.13: Woe to them, for they have turned away from me; ruin to them, for they have rebelled against me. Yet I will redeem them, but they speak falsehoods against me.
verses.14: And their hearts did not cry to me, but they wailed in their beds, over grain and wine they were cut off; they rebelled against me.
verses.15: I have disciplined them strongly, I have strengthened their arms, and yet they thought evil toward me.
verses.16: They returned not, they became like a bent bow; their rulers will fall by the sword because of the anger of their tongues. This is their disgrace in the land of Egypt.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: The metaphor of the furnace and baking is complex. "Feeding on fat until it is leavened" reflects the imagery of a furnace heated by the baker, which may involve a process of leavening dough. The metaphor is kept intact in English, with a natural rendering.
- v. 10: "The glory of Israel" refers to the dignity or status of the northern kingdom, not a specific temple or place. The phrase is rendered in a way that reflects its symbolic meaning.
- v. 16: "This is their disgrace in the land of Egypt" is a concluding statement that refers to their eventual humiliation, likely in exile. The reference to Egypt may be symbolic or literal.
